evidence: deepseek checks `if p1 + p2 > T` and then `total1`/`total2`; gpt-oss stores `p1 + p2 > T` and checks `sum1`; qwen checks `p1 + p2 > T` and `total_p1`; glm uses the same three sums
affordance_in_statement: For an individual item, the conditions are duration, `S_{i,2} >= E_{i,1}`, and `S_{i,1} >= 0`, `E_{i,2} <= T`; for a machine, the only requirements are duration, non-overlap, and `S_{i,c} >= 0`, `E_{i,c} <= T`.
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task: these formal constraints intrinsically reduce to `p1+p2>T` for JOB and `sum(p_c)>T` for LOAD. Re-presenting the explanatory parentheticals can hide the shortcut, but cannot eliminate it without changing the scheduling model.

common_affordance: The certificate definitions deliberately decouple the constraints, so validity is determined entirely by additive duration lower bounds: `p1+p2>T` for a job or `sum(p_c)>T` for a machine.
recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors. A genuine defeat would require changing the model by adding an order-dependent or item-dependent setup/transfer constraint between operations, so feasibility is no longer determined solely by these additive sums.
